t:
(a) In General.—Section 1317 of the Federal Housing Enterprises Financial Safety and Soundness Act of 1992 (12 U.S.C. 4517) is amended—
        (1) in subsection (a), by striking “enterprise” each place that term appears and inserting “regulated entity”; 
        (2) in subsection (b)—
            (A) by inserting “of a regulated entity” after “under this section”; and 
            (B) by striking “to determine the condition of an enterprise for the purpose of ensuring its financial safety and soundness” and inserting “or appropriate”;  
        (3) in subsection (c), in the second sentence, by inserting before the period “to conduct examinations under this section”; 
        (4) by redesignating subsections (d) through (f) as subsections (e) through (g), respectively; and 
        (5) by inserting after subsection (c) the following:“(d) Inspector General.—There shall be within the Agency an Inspector General, who shall be appointed in accordance with section 3(a) of the Inspector General Act of 1978.”.  
    (b) Direct Hire Authority To Hire Accountants, Economists, and Examiners.—Section 1317 of the Federal Housing Enterprises Financial Safety and Soundness Act of 1992 (12 U.S.C. 4517) is amended by adding at the end the following:“(h) Appointment of Accountants, Economists, and Examiners.—“(1) Applicability.—This section shall apply with respect to any position of examiner, accountant, economist, and specialist in financial markets and in technology at the Agency, with respect to supervision and regulation of the regulated entities, that is in the competitive service.“(2) Appointment authority.—The Director may appoint candidates to any position described in paragraph (1)—“(A) in accordance with the statutes, rules, and regulations governing appointments in the excepted service; and“(B) notwithstanding any statutes, rules, and regulations governing appointments in the competitive service.”. 
    (c) Amendments to Inspector General Act.—Section 11 of the Inspector General Act of 1978 (5 U.S.C. App.) is amended—
        (1) in paragraph (1), by inserting “; the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency” after “Social Security Administration”; and 
        (2) in paragraph (2), by inserting “, the Federal Housing Finance Agency” after “Social Security Administration”.  
    (d) Authority To Contract for Reviews of Regulated Entities.—Section 1319 of the Federal Housing Enterprises Financial Safety and Soundness Act of 1992 (12 U.S.C. 4519) is amended—
        (1) in the section heading, by striking “enterprises by rating organization” and inserting “regulated entities”; and 
        (2) by striking “enterprises” and inserting “regulated entities”.  
    (e) Office of the Ombudsman.—Section 1317 of the Federal Housing Enterprises Financial Safety and Soundness Act of 1992 (12 U.S.C. 4517) is amended by adding at the end the following:“(i) Ombudsman.—The Director shall establish, by regulation, an Office of the Ombudsman within the Agency, which shall be responsible for considering complaints and appeals, from any regulated entity and any person that has a business relationship with a regulated entity, regarding any matter relating to the regulation and supervision of such regulated entity by the Agency. The regulation issued by the Director under this subsection shall specify the authority and duties of the Office of the Ombudsman.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this section is purely internal agency housekeeping (examiners, Inspector General, hiring authority, conforming amendments), which would be "No". But subsection (e) requires the Director to act "by regulation", and a rulemaking requirement counts as participation under the definition. The Ombudsman it creates also gives regulated entities and their business partners, who are outside the federal government, a formal channel to file complaints and appeals about the Agency's regulation and supervision.
fable.s: The Director shall establish, by regulation, an Office of the Ombudsman within the Agency, which shall be responsible for considering complaints and appeals, from any regulated entity and any person that has a business relationship with a regulated entity, regarding any matter relating to the regulation and supervision of such regulated entity by the Agency.

qwen_block.w: The section primarily deals with internal agency structure, hiring authority, and the establishment of an internal Office of the Ombudsman. While the Ombudsman considers complaints from outside parties, this is an internal administrative grievance mechanism, not a participatory process like an advisory board, public hearing, or consultation before a decision. The definition excludes applications and internal administrative processes, and the other subsections involve only federal officials or technical statutory amendments.
qwen_block.s: (e) Office of the Ombudsman.—Section 1317 of the Federal Housing Enterprises Financial Safety and Soundness Act of 1992 (12 U.S.C. 4517) is amended by adding at the end the following:“(i) Ombudsman.—The Director shall establish, by regulation, an Office of the Ombudsman within the Agency, which shall be responsible for considering complaints and appeals, from any regulated entity and any person that has a business relationship with a regulated entity, regarding any matter relating to the regulation and supervision of such regulated entity by the Agency. The regulation issued by the Director under this subsection shall specify the authority and duties of the Office of the Ombudsman.”.
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the creation of an "Office of the Ombudsman" to consider complaints from "any person" constitutes participation because it involves outside parties interacting with the government. However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants" and generally treats internal administrative grievance mechanisms (like ombudsman offices or appeals processes for specific regulatory decisions) as internal government functions rather than the kind of consultative participation (like advisory boards or public comment periods) defined here. The ombudsman is an internal office established by the Director to handle complaints, not a mechanism for the public to consult with the government *before* a decision is made or to participate in policy formation. The other parts of the section deal with internal hiring authority, inspector general appointments, and technical amendments to existing statutes, none of which involve outside participation.

opus.w: Subsection (e) requires the Director to act 'by regulation,' and the definition counts required rulemaking as participation. The Ombudsman office also gives regulated entities and private parties a formal way to complain about and appeal the agency's supervisory decisions. The Inspector General and hiring provisions are purely internal, but they do not cancel out the rulemaking and outside-party appeal channel in (e).
opus.s: The Director shall establish, by regulation, an Office of the Ombudsman within the Agency, which shall be responsible for considering complaints and appeals, from any regulated entity and any person that has a business relationship with a regulated entity, regarding any matter relating to the regulation and supervision of such regulated entity by the Agency.
opus.b:
1. **The tempting wrong reading:** Most of this section is internal housekeeping. It renames terms, creates an Inspector General, gives the agency hiring authority, and amends the Inspector General Act. All of that stays inside the federal government, so it is tempting to answer "No."
2. **Why that fails:** Subsection (e) requires the Director to set up the Ombudsman office "by regulation." The definition counts required rulemaking as participation. The office will also hear complaints and appeals from regulated entities and private parties, so outsiders get a formal channel to object to agency decisions. That crosses the federal boundary, so the answer is "Yes."

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes an internal Office of the Ombudsman to handle complaints and appeals from regulated entities. This is an internal administrative grievance mechanism, not a process for outside parties to consult with or coordinate with the government before a decision is made. It does not involve public comment periods, advisory boards with outside members, or consultation with states/tribes prior to action.
qwen_chat.s: (e) Office of the Ombudsman.—Section 1317 of the Federal Housing Enterprises Financial Safety and Soundness Act of 1992 (12 U.S.C. 4517) is amended by adding at the end the following:“(i) Ombudsman.—The Director shall establish, by regulation, an Office of the Ombudsman within the Agency, which shall be responsible for considering complaints and appeals, from any regulated entity and any person that has a business relationship with a regulated entity, regarding any matter relating to the regulation and supervision of such regulated entity by the Agency. The regulation issued by the Director under this subsection shall specify the authority and duties of the Office of the Ombudsman.”.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it establishes an Office of the Ombudsman to handle complaints from regulated entities and other persons.
Resolution: An ombudsman is an internal agency office that handles administrative complaints and appeals. It does not involve consultation or coordination with outside parties *before* a federal decision is made, nor does it grant a right to sue or participate in rulemaking. It is an internal grievance mechanism.
